Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the rear-end collision you
were involved in in Houston, Texas. Before we begin, do you consent to this conversation being recorded?
A: Yes, I consent.
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just go by the claimant on file, if that's okay.
Q: That's acceptable. Can you describe where you were and what you were doing when the collision happened?
A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road in the city, waiting to turn. I had been stopped for maybe ten or fifteen
seconds when I felt a hard jolt from behind.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?
A: No. I was looking ahead at the light. The first thing I noticed was the impact and the sound of metal.
Q: Were you able to drive your vehicle from the scene?
A: Yes, it was drivable, but the rear bumper was pushed in and the trunk wouldn't close properly.
Q: Have you sought medical attention since the collision?
A: Yes. I went to an urgent care clinic that same afternoon. They diagnosed whiplash and told me to expect stiffness
in my neck and upper back for several weeks.
Q: How are you feeling today?
A: My neck still aches, especially when I turn my head to check my blind spot. I've also had headaches a few times a
week, and I've been taking over-the-counter pain relievers.
Q: Have you missed any work because of your injuries?
A: I missed two days and had to shift some of my duties to a coworker while I recover.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm following the treatment plan and I'm willing to provide my medical records.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
